items.statement: The EQ-TIPS descriptive system had little missing data and no floor effects in the hospital groups, but the VAS had more missing responses.
source: Full article, Results—Performance of EQ-TIPS across condition groups, first paragraph; Discussion, second paragraph

items.statement: Pain responses, the EQ-TIPS level sum score, and the 111111 ceiling state discriminated health groups, whereas the VAS did not discriminate general health between groups.

values.direction: Significant difference in level sum score

source: Full article, Abstract—Results; Results—Performance of EQ-TIPS across condition groups; Table 2; Figure 1

items.statement: All hypothesized concurrent-validity relationships were weak to moderate and significant; the strongest highlighted relationship was between EQ-TIPS pain and FLACC pain.
source: Full article, Results—Concurrent validity of the EQ-TIPS dimensions; Table 3

items.statement: EQ-TIPS dimension levels explained little variance in the VAS score, and none of the dimension coefficients was statistically significant.

values.denominator: 163 participants after nine outliers were excluded

source: Full article, Results—Performance of the EQ-TIPS General Health Question measured on the VAS; Table 4

items.statement: Movement, play, pain, and eating had statistically significant one-week agreement. Relationships, communication, and the level sum score did not. The VAS had an ICC of 0.72.
source: Full article, Results—Test-retest reliability; Table 5

items.statement: Cognitive-interview participants reported no comprehension problems, so the researchers made no changes to the isiXhosa consensus version.

values.direction: No reported comprehension problems and no resulting changes

source: Full article, Methods—Measures—EQ-TIPS, cognitive-interview paragraphs

items.statement: The authors conclude that the isiXhosa EQ-TIPS is feasible, valid, and reliable for very young children in South Africa, with caveats concerning understanding and performance of general health and the VAS.
source: Full article, Discussion, opening paragraph; Conclusion

items.statement: The authors suggest that the isiXhosa EQ-TIPS be included in assessments of children with health conditions in this context and recommend further research on age effects, responsiveness, and understanding of the VAS.
source: Full article, Abstract—Conclusion; Conclusion

items.statement: The crèche and hospital groups differed in child age and caregiver composition, which made it difficult to separate age effects from health-group effects.
source: Full article, Discussion, opening paragraph and age-performance paragraph

items.statement: Independent completion may have been difficult for some crèche caregivers, and researcher availability differed between crèche and hospital settings.
source: Full article, Discussion, opening paragraph

items.statement: The VAS or the term health may have been poorly understood; cognitive debriefing involved only ten caregivers, and many caregivers did not know their child's health condition.
source: Full article, Discussion, general-health and VAS paragraph

items.statement: Age-related performance was difficult to establish because age distributions differed by health group and the inpatient and outpatient diagnoses were heterogeneous.
source: Full article, Discussion, age-performance paragraph

items.statement: Reasons for changes in dimension responses were not recorded, and the healthy crèche retest sample provided limited variation in reported problems.
source: Full article, Discussion, test-retest paragraph
